input: This executive summary delves into an exciting opportunity to enhance energy efficiency at the food plant through a proposed heat-recovery retrofit, and it presents a comprehensive overview of the projected benefits, costs, and recommended next steps. The plant currently uses a substantial 2089 MWh of electricity per year in refrigeration, making refrigeration a key focus area for improvement. According to the equipment vendor, the retrofit is projected to save 12% of that electricity use, which corresponds to a derived saving of 251 MWh per year at the vendor figure. The capital cost of the retrofit is $368k, and at an electricity price of $0.11 per kWh, the derived annual saving works out to $28k, giving a derived simple payback of 13.1 years. It is important to note that the saving figure is a vendor projection and was not measured at this plant, and refrigeration load in the summer peak month was not modelled, so the projections should be treated with a degree of caution. In light of these considerations, it is recommended that a metered trial be carried out on one of the three refrigeration lines before any capital decision is taken, in order to validate the projected savings under real operating conditions. The plant engineer will own the trial and will be responsible for reporting its findings.
target: The recommendation is a metered trial of the heat-recovery retrofit on one of the three refrigeration lines, before any capital decision. The plant engineer owns the trial. The plant uses 2089 MWh of electricity per year in refrigeration. The equipment vendor projects a saving of 12% of that use, a derived saving of 251 MWh per year at the vendor figure. Against a capital cost of $368k, the derived annual saving is $28k at an electricity price of $0.11 per kWh, and the derived simple payback is 13.1 years. The trade-off is therefore a long payback resting on an unverified figure: the saving is a vendor projection and was not measured at this plant, and refrigeration load in the summer peak month was not modelled. A metered trial on one line replaces the projection with a measurement at this plant, on one of the three lines whose combined use the retrofit would address. The capital decision should wait for the trial result, since the payback is long enough that a shortfall in the measured saving would change the decision. The trial is a measurement exercise on one line, run ahead of the capital commitment, and its result is the evidence the capital decision currently lacks. The trial also tests the retrofit against the plant's own refrigeration load pattern, which the vendor projection does not use. Until the trial reports, every figure in this summary is the vendor's figure or a derivation from it, and the saving at this plant is unknown.
